Type 2 Diabetes

Condition / Protocol
50g is genuinely ketogenic and is the current target here. The stricter sub-20g level is the more rigorously studied "classic" therapeutic threshold in the research literature — it's the level that would typically be moved to if recurrence or progression occurred, not the default starting point. It's not used as the baseline here because sustained adherence at that level is genuinely difficult: food and drink choices become significantly more restricted, and long-term sustainability becomes a real concern. Discuss any change to either target with your care team.

Weight Phase History
Tell the AI about intentional weight phases so it interprets trends correctly.
Example: first line 2026-03-12 loss means intentional loss from data start. Second line 2026-06-21 gain means gaining phase from that date.
Condition History
Logs automatically whenever you change condition above. Lets reports filter to a specific condition period using that period's own real targets, rather than today's, when it differs.
Example: first line 2026-01-15 general means General Health from data start. Second line 2026-06-01 migraine means Migraine protocol from that date onward.
Activity Level History
Logs automatically whenever your Activity Level changes, whether you change it above or it auto-switches from sustained real step data. Keeps later changes from retroactively distorting how old logged days get interpreted.
Example: first line 2026-01-15 moderate means Moderately Active from data start. Second line 2026-06-01 active means Very Active from that date onward.

⚡ Suggested Targets
Enter height, age, sex and weight to generate suggestions.
Daily calorie target
Daily protein target (g)
Daily fat target (g)
⚠ What changing these numbers actually does ▸
Calories set the pace, not the destination. Since protein and carbs stay fixed, moving your calorie/fat target changes how big your daily surplus is — that's what controls how fast you gain, not whether the weight is "good" weight. Roughly: ~250–400kcal/day surplus is a slow, controlled gain (~0.2–0.4kg/week); 500kcal+ is faster but increasingly likely to add more fat than lean tissue.

Fat % here is a ketosis requirement, not a body-composition lever. The high fat percentage exists to maintain therapeutic ketosis — it doesn't drive muscle growth. Protein plus resistance training does that. A ketogenic macro split isn't optimised for lean-mass gain the way a moderate-carb bulk would be; without a training stimulus, surplus calories default toward fat regardless of the macro split.

If you're logging Strength Training, that consistent stimulus is what shifts a given surplus toward more muscle and less fat — the macro numbers alone can't do that on their own.

If you're unsure, smaller changes are safer than bigger ones. A modest adjustment you can observe over a week or two beats a large jump you have to guess the effect of.

Carb counting method
Total (the default) shows the raw carbs figure exactly as printed on the label — polyols (sugar alcohols like erythritol, xylitol) are still counted in full, since that's how UK/EU labels state the number. Net subtracts polyols from that figure, giving the lower, physiologically-relevant number — this is what a "keto" product with, say, 16g total carbs is actually relying on: most of that is polyols the label counts but your body barely responds to. Fibre isn't subtracted separately here, unlike US-style net carb calculations — UK/EU labels already exclude fibre from the printed carbs figure before it reaches this app (fibre is its own separate line on the label, not part of the carbohydrate total the way US labelling includes it), so subtracting it again would double-count something already excluded. If Total ever looks too high for something clearly marketed as keto/low-carb, that's the sign Net is what you actually want to be looking at. Switching only affects today's ceiling check reliably; older logged days may not have polyol data recorded, so this can't be safely applied retroactively.

📐 Formulas & Technical Reference ▾ hide
BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate)
Formula used:
Manual body fat % (fallback)
If a connected smart scale is syncing body fat data, that's used automatically and takes priority over this. Not everyone has one — this manual figure is the fallback for anyone who doesn't, and stays in effect until synced data appears. Leave both blank and this falls back to Mifflin-St Jeor entirely — Katch-McArdle needs a real body fat figure to mean anything, not a guess.
Mifflin-St Jeor —
Men: 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age + 5
Women: 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age − 161

Harris-Benedict (revised) —
Men: 88.362 + 13.397 × weight(kg) + 4.799 × height(cm) − 5.677 × age
Women: 447.593 + 9.247 × weight(kg) + 3.098 × height(cm) − 4.330 × age

Katch-McArdle —
370 + 21.6 × lean body mass(kg), where lean body mass = weight × (1 − body fat% ÷ 100)
All three need height, age, and sex set in Profile (Katch-McArdle also needs body fat %) — falls back to a generic estimate otherwise.
TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure)
TDEE = BMR × activity multiplier
Multiplier derived from your 30-day average steps:
>12,000 steps/day → ×1.725 (very active)
>8,000 steps/day → ×1.55 (active)
>5,000 steps/day → ×1.375 (lightly active)
≤5,000 steps/day → ×1.2 (sedentary)
Recalculated fresh every time — always reflects your current 30-day average, not a fixed setting.
Exercise Calories (MET-based)
kcal = MET value × weight(kg) × duration(hours)
MET values by activity and effort (Easy / Moderate / Hard):
Walking: 2.8 / 3.5 / 4.5  ·  Resistance: 3.0 / 5.0 / 6.0
Cycling: 4.0 / 6.8 / 10.0  ·  Running: 8.3 / 9.8 / 11.8
Swimming: 6.0 / 8.3 / 9.8  ·  Rowing: 4.8 / 7.0 / 8.5
Once you've logged enough sessions alongside real wearable calorie data, a personal calibration factor is applied on top of the raw MET formula — the raw, uncalibrated figure is always kept separately so the calibration itself never drifts against an already-adjusted number.
Walking Pace Bands (fitness-adjusted)
Effort = pace ≤ easyMax ? Easy : pace ≤ moderateMax ? Moderate : Hard
Bands by your Activity Level setting (Profile → Activity Level):
Sedentary: Easy ≤2.0mph, Moderate ≤2.75mph
Lightly active: Easy ≤2.5mph, Moderate ≤3.25mph
Moderately active: Easy ≤3.0mph, Moderate ≤3.75mph
Very active: Easy ≤3.5mph, Moderate ≤3.75mph, above is Hard
No single universal mph threshold for "brisk" walking actually exists — the AHA (≥2.5mph) and CDC (≥3.5mph) officially disagree, explicitly because it depends on individual fitness. The active tier here is anchored on the CDC figure, light on the AHA figure. Used both to auto-suggest an effort label from a logged pace, and in reverse to estimate calories/steps when only an effort label (not exact pace) is available — previously these were two separate, inconsistent hardcoded values; now both read from the same source. Long-duration walks (4+ miles, scaling with activity level) get bumped up a level, since sustained effort is harder than pace alone suggests.

Known limitation: the MET calorie values above (2.8/3.5/4.5 for walking) are not yet adjusted the same way — they were calibrated assuming something close to the old universal pace scale, so calorie estimates specifically for non-"moderately active" tiers may be slightly off until this gets addressed too.
Activity Level Auto-Switch
Tier = 30-day avg steps >12,000 active · >8,000 moderate · >5,000 light · else sedentary
Same thresholds the existing TDEE activity multiplier already uses — one definition of each tier, not two that could disagree. For each of the last N days (Auto-Switch Threshold, default 14, shared with the weight/goal auto-switch above), computes what the rolling 30-day step average would have suggested as of that day. If all N of those daily-computed averages agree on one tier that differs from your current Activity Level setting, it switches automatically — walking pace bands and calorie/TDEE targets update immediately.

Deliberately checks the smoothed 30-day average at each point rather than each single day's raw step count — steps are naturally far noisier day-to-day than a weight trend, so requiring every individual day to match would let one low-step rest day break an otherwise genuine, sustained improvement.

A move to a more active tier shows a celebration (matching ketosis streak milestones); a move to a less active tier is a plain, factual notification only — informed either way, celebrated only when it's genuinely something to celebrate. Every switch is logged to Activity Level History (Profile), so a later change never retroactively distorts how older logged days get interpreted.
Macro Ratio %
Protein kcal = protein(g) × 4
Fat kcal = fat(g) × 9
Carb kcal = carbs(g) × 4
Each macro's % = its kcal ÷ total kcal × 100
Fat (when not directly recorded)
fat(g) = max(0, (kcal − protein×4 − carbs×4)) ÷ 9
Back-calculated from the balance of calories once protein and carbs are accounted for — only used when a logged item genuinely has no fat value of its own.
Net Carbs (optional setting)
net carbs = total carbs − polyols
Off by default (shows total/gross carbs). Deliberately does not also subtract fibre — UK/EU labels already exclude fibre from the printed carbs figure before it reaches this app (fibre is its own separate line, not part of the carbohydrate total the way US labelling includes it), so subtracting it again would double-count something already excluded. Only reliably applied to recent days with real polyol data recorded — older days may not have it.
Carb Ceilings & Ketosis Adherence
Every day is judged against its own logged mode's ceiling — Standard, Occasion, or Holiday — each independently configurable above. A holiday day within its own (wider) ceiling counts as fully compliant; it is never compared against the Standard ceiling.
Exercise Offset for Carb Overage
overage kcal = (actual carbs − ceiling) × 4
addressed if: exercise kcal that day ≥ overage kcal × threshold%
Off by default. Never changes whether a day counts as over ceiling — purely an additional, separate classification. See the Exercise Offset settings card above.
Non-Walking Steps & Baseline
Your daily step baseline (default 7,500, set above) represents ordinary day-to-day movement assumed already accounted for. Steps beyond a logged walk's own estimated count, and beyond this baseline, are credited as additional "Easy effort" activity calories — steps within the baseline add nothing extra, since that's the assumption already built into your calorie target.

Idle Timeout ▾ hide
Pauses the app's own background activity (notification checks, chart updates) after a period with no taps, scrolls, or typing - genuinely reduces what the app is doing while you're not actually using it, rather than it quietly running in the background the whole time the tab is open. Nothing you've typed or logged is ever lost - it's a pause, not a reset.
Timeout after (minutes)
Default 5 minutes. A countdown appears once you're genuinely idle (not during active use), with a warning before the pause actually happens.

⚠ Local server not running
The MaxedHealth local server has stopped. This usually happens because:
  • Your phone restarted and Termux:Boot didn't auto-start it yet
  • The server process was killed to free memory
Open Termux and type:
mhstart
The sync button will go green within a few seconds.
Important: Keep Termux open in the background — minimise it with the home button, don't swipe it away. Swiping Termux away stops the server.
On reboot, the server restarts automatically via Termux:Boot.
